title: "globato gui" missing dependencies, and a file-permissions bug.

labels.name: dependencies
labels.description: Pull requests that update a dependency file

body:
**OS:** Ubuntu 26.06
**Python:** 3.12.7

The latest source code that includes the "globato gui" command is missing some dependencies. It may be that these are considered "optional" dependencies that are only needed if you want to use the "globato gui" feature, but that should be clearly stated in an error message. Just a text-error stating "No module named voila" with an exit makes it unclear to a user whether it's a bug ("this software is broken") or an explicitly-intended feature. It exited gracefully on the first dependency error but didn't indicate to the user this behavior was intended.

- `voila`
- `lxml[html_clean]` (conda)
- `lxml_html_clean` (PyPI)

^ The `lxml_html_clean` dependency error (encounterd only after voila is successfully installed) causes a traceback error, not a graceful exit.

After both these dependencies are fixed, the following error is encountered:
```
$ globato gui
Starting Globato Web Server...
A browser window will open shortly at http://localhost:8866/
Press Ctrl+C in this terminal to stop the server.
[Voila] Using /tmp to store connection files
[Voila] Storing connection files in /tmp/voila_1uf76oec.
[Voila] Serving static files from /home/mmacferrin/miniconda3/envs/ivert/lib/python3.12/site-packages/voila/static.
[Voila] Voilà is running at:
http://localhost:8866/
[Voila] WARNING | Notebook globato_gui_temp.ipynb is not trusted
[Voila] WARNING | Native kernel (python3) is not available
500 GET / (127.0.0.1): No Jupyter kernel for language 'python' found
500 GET / (127.0.0.1) 223.34ms
403 GET /voila/files/favicon.ico (127.0.0.1): File not allowlisted
403 GET /voila/files/favicon.ico (127.0.0.1) 1.67ms
```
I've gotten no further than that.

**RECOMMENDED:** Install globato in a clean environment. Iteratively fix dependencies and file permissions until `globato gui` runs without error, and/or with a clear message about needed optional-feature dependencies.

title: Avoid zero-filling per-file source masks
body:
## Description

# Avoid zero-filling per-file source masks

## Summary

Avoid explicitly zero-filling each per-file source-mask raster when it is created.

Source masks are created as `uint8` GeoTIFFs with `nodata=0`. Unwritten pixels already read as zero, and populated windows are subsequently updated by the existing source-mask logic. The explicit full-raster zero write is therefore unnecessary.

This removes:

```python
dst.write(np.zeros((1, self.ycount, self.xcount), dtype="uint8"))
```

while preserving the existing per-file source-mask and provenance behavior.

## Validation

I tested the change with a real `coupling-bathy-topo` build over a 0.075° × 0.075° Southern California area at 1/9 arc-second resolution.

The A/B/A2 comparison used:

- **A:** original implementation
- **B:** explicit zero-fill removed
- **A2:** original implementation again with a warm cache

The test processed 125 source records, including 120 DAV lidar files.

Exact-equivalence checks showed:

- 125/125 individual per-file source masks identical
- final DEM identical
- stack raster identical
- Transformez grids identical
- provenance coverage identical
- VRT semantically identical
- GPKG semantically identical
- QML identical
- 132/132 audit entries semantically identical after normalizing only runtime timestamps, run-directory paths, and equivalent tuple/list serialization of identical bounds

Source identity, weights, uncertainty values, and per-file provenance were unchanged.

## Performance

The small end-to-end test was intentionally sized for fast regression testing, and whole-build timing was within normal run-to-run I/O variability:

- A: 610 s
- B: 614 s
- A2: 604 s

Because the removed operation scales with both raster size and number of per-file masks, its contribution is too small to resolve reliably in this small test area.

I therefore also benchmarked the source-mask initialization operation directly using the actual source-mask raster profile on the same filesystem:

- 30 masks per trial
- 8100 × 8100 cells per mask
- 3 rounds with alternating baseline/optimized order

Results:

- explicit zero-fill median: **4.194 s**
- no explicit zero-fill median: **0.028 s**
- median time saved: **4.166 s per 30 masks**
- component improvement: **99.34%**
- component speedup: **150.8×**
- resulting raster structure and pixel values: **exactly equivalent**

This corresponds to approximately 0.139 s of unnecessary initialization per production-sized source mask. For a build with ~1,322 per-file masks, that is roughly 184 seconds (~3.1 minutes) of avoidable initialization work on the tested filesystem.

title: Clarify ICESat-2 water/seafloor class labels
body:
## Summary

Relabels the `ATL03Reader` photon classes in `meta_desc` so each water class clearly states whether it represents a surface or the floor:

| Code | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 40 | Bathymetry | Seafloor |
| 41 | Coastline / Nearshore Water | Nearshore Water Surface |
| 42 | Inland Water | Inland Water Surface |
| 44 | Open Ocean | Open Ocean Surface |

## Motivation

- "Coastline" was conceptually unclear as a label for a photon class.
- The ocean classes did not clearly distinguish surface returns from the seafloor. With these labels, every water surface is explicitly a "Surface" and 40 is unambiguously the floor.

The class codes are unchanged; only the human-readable labels in the docstring are updated.

title: Drop the fiona dependency in favor of pyogrio/geopandas
body:
## Motivation

globato hard-requires `fiona`, and that is now the last place the continuous-dems stack can force users into a from-source GDAL build. It surfaced concretely in ivert CI this week (continuous-dems/ivert#38, part of continuous-dems/ivert#21): on Python 3.14 there is no fiona binary wheel (fiona 1.10.1 ships wheels only through cp313), so `pip install ivert` → globato → fiona falls back to a source build and dies with:

```
WARNING:root:Failed to get options via gdal-config: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'gdal-config'
CRITICAL:root:A GDAL API version must be specified. Provide a path to gdal-config using a GDAL_CONFIG environment variable or use a GDAL_VERSION environment variable.
```

This is exactly the ease-of-install problem the org has been eliminating (ivert has now removed all of its own gdal/ogr/osr usage). Any platform/Python combination that fiona doesn't ship a wheel for — currently including all of Python 3.14 — hits this wall, and Windows users are the most likely victims. fiona is also in maintenance mode upstream, so its wheel coverage will keep lagging new Python releases.

## Suggested replacement

`pyogrio` covers fiona's vector I/O role with the same OGR format support, vendors its own GDAL (no system binaries or headers needed), ships wheels promptly for new Python versions, and is already the default I/O engine underneath `geopandas` — which globato's dependents (e.g. ivert) already use. For most read/write call sites, `geopandas.read_file()` / `GeoDataFrame.to_file()` is a near drop-in; for schema-level or record-streaming work, `pyogrio.read_dataframe` / `pyogrio.write_dataframe` and `pyogrio.read_info` cover the rest.

## Current fiona usage

`import fiona` appears in these modules (as of v0.2.14 / current main):

- `streams/readers/fio.py` (the generic vector reader)
- `streams/readers/icesat2.py`
- `modules/osm_landmask.py`
- `modules/glob_coast.py`
- `hooks/rasters/base.py`
- `hooks/rasters/polygonize.py`
- `hooks/vectors/fill_holes.py`
- `hooks/filters/vector_crop.py`
- `hooks/tools/osm_landmask.py`
- `utils.py` (CRS extraction helper, one deferred import)

Happy to help with the migration if useful.

title: Fix ATL24 bathy photon heights to respect requested vertical_datum
body:
## Summary
- `apply_atl24_classifications()` in the ATL03 reader was writing ATL24's `ortho_h` (a tide-free EGM2008 orthometric height) straight into `photon_height`, ignoring the reader's requested `vertical_datum`.
- Every other photon class (ground, canopy, ice, etc.) is converted between ellipsoid/geoid/mean-tide frames in `read_atl03()` based on `vertical_datum`, so bathy_floor (class 40) photons ended up silently geoid-referenced inside output whose metadata claims one consistent datum for the whole granule.
- In areas with large geoid undulation, this produced bathymetry photon heights offset by tens of meters relative to the surrounding ground/canopy photons and the DEM being validated against (confirmed against a Fiji test case with ~50 m undulation, where bathy photons appeared ~55 m too deep before this fix).

## Fix
- `read_atl03()` now retains each photon's geoid undulation and tide correction terms (`photon_geoid`, `photon_f2m`, `photon_tide_f2m`) so they survive the merge into `apply_atl24_classifications()`.
- `apply_atl24_classifications()` converts ATL24's `ortho_h` into whichever `vertical_datum` was requested (ellipsoid, ellipsoid-mean-tide, geoid, geoid-mean-tide) using the same algebra already applied to non-bathy photons, before overwriting `photon_height`.
- The helper columns are dropped again before `read_atl03()` returns, so the reader's public output schema is unchanged.

## Test plan
- [x] Re-ran against a real Fiji ATL03/ATL24 granule pair with a downstream DEM-validation pipeline; bathy_floor heights now land in the same vertical frame as ground photons instead of being offset by the local geoid undulation.

title: glob_coast: add osm_water source, unify voting, progress logging, Unzip hook
body:
## Summary

- **`osm_water` source**: new source that runs `osm_landmask` with `include_water=True`, carving OSM lake/river polygons out of the land vote rather than counting them as land. Uses its own `outdir` so its cache doesn't collide with `osm_landmask`.
- **Unified `_apply_source_votes`**: replaces the separate `_process_raster` / `_process_vector` methods. All files for a source are processed together before writing to `self.grid`, which fixes double-counting when multiple overlapping tiles from the same source cover the same pixel. Vector reads now use `src.filter(bbox=...)` to skip out-of-region geometries before rasterization.
- **Progress logging**: each source now logs `[TAG]`-prefixed status lines (found/fetching/ready) and errors.
- **`Unzip` hook**: added to the general (non-NHD) fetch path.

> **Deferred to future PRs:** Shapefile spatial index (`_ensure_shp_spatial_index`) and NHD tile caching (`_scan_source_dir`) were removed from this PR to keep scope focused. They can be added independently.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `glob_coast` with `sources=osm_water,hydrolakes,copernicus` over a region with significant inland water bodies and verify lakes/rivers are masked as water
- [ ] Run with `sources=osm_landmask,...` and confirm behavior is unchanged from before
- [ ] Confirm `[TAG]` progress lines appear in logs for each source
